### Async API reservations cannot be cleared by web-History absence
For the current self-hosted Pangram async API route, authenticated web History is not an adjudicator of whether a paid API submission occurred. A known-success async API control was absent from the same History surface that also failed to find the ambiguous Shaking scan. Therefore absence is non-evidence for repeat authorization: keep the reservation counted and blocked unless durable task-id/cache/ledger evidence or another transport-appropriate exact record resolves it. Before using History absence for any transport, validate the surface with a known-success positive control from that same transport/configuration. Read-only recovery must remain mechanically unable to POST.
